items.prose: The quarter unit circle is $y = \sqrt{1 - x^2}$ on $[0, 1]$, with $f'(x) = \frac{-x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$. Then $1 + f'(x)^2 = \frac{1}{1 - x^2}$, so its length is $\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$. The integrand is unbounded at $x = 1$.
